blocks.text: did, they pledged their allegiance to him.[^1]

According to a narration reported by Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ka'b (RA), Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Ansaar (after they had pledged their allegiance), "Leave for your camps." It was then that Hadhrat Abbaas bin Ubaadah (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that if you wish, we shall attack the people at Mina with our swords by tomorrow." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "You have not been commanded to do this. You may however leave for your camps."[^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that when Rasulullaah ﷺ went to the trench (before the Battle of Ahzaab) early one morning, he found the Muhaajireen and Ansaar digging in the cold because they had no slaves to do the work for them. When he saw the fatigue and hunger they were suffering, he said:

blocks.arabic_text: اَللّٰهُمَّ اِنَّ الْعَيْشَ عَيْشُ الْاٰخِرَهْ ۞ فَاغْفِرِ الْاَنْصَارَ وَالْمُهَاجِرَهْ
blocks.text:
"O Allaah! There is no life but the life of the Aakhirah
Do forgive the Ansaar and the Muhaajirah (the Muhaajireen)"
In response to this, the Sahabah (RA) said:

blocks.arabic_text: نَحْنُ الَّذِيْنَ بَايَعُوْا مُحَمَّدًا ۞ عَلَى الْجِهَادِ مَا بَقِيْنَا اَبَدًا
blocks.text:
"We are those who have pledged allegiance to Muhammad
Pledged to wage Jihaad as long as we are alive"[^3]

The Hadith of Hadhrat Mujaashi (RA) has already passed[^4] which states that when Hadhrat Mujaashi (RA) asked what was it that he could pledge his allegiance to, Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Pledge your allegiance to Islaam and to Jihaad."

Similarly, the Hadith of Hadhrat Basheer bin Khasaasiyyah (RA) has also passed[^5] in which Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Basheer! By virtue of what deed will you enter Jannah without Zakaah and Jihaad?" Hadhrat Basheer then said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Extend your hand." When Rasulullaah ﷺ did so, Hadhrat Basheer (RA) pledged his allegiance to all the actions.

In the same regard, the Hadith of Hadhrat Ya'la bin Munyah (RA) has passed[^6] in which he said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Allow my father to pledge that he will undertake the Hijrah." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "I shall rather allow him to pledge his allegiance to Jihaad."
